implementerProof.how: Four of the architect's five items hold and I checked each by driving it rather than reading it: item 2's file-set is fully accounted across all three forward merges, item 3's migration question is answered empirically with the real stamps, item 4's .github/changelog-packages exists with packages/daemon=legion-v, and item 5's CI is read from GitHub. Item 1 was short by one status, which I closed myself with a test commit rather than reporting as owed. The round fails on a defect I found outside the item list: TestOnlyTheStepsTheProviderRefusedAreReportedRefused, added by this branch at f5ed98ce5, fails 19 times in 100 runs of one reproducible command, so this change puts a nondeterministically red test into the suite.

failures.criterion: A1 / R1 - the tests this change adds pass against the change. A test of this branch's own new code must give the same answer every run, or CI's red says nothing about the branch and a reviewer reading it learns to discount it.
failures.evidence: packages/daemon/internal/claudebridge/turnoutcome_test.go:127 TestOnlyTheStepsTheProviderRefusedAreReportedRefused, added by this branch's own commit f5ed98ce5 (round five), is racy. Command: cd packages/daemon && go test ./internal/claudebridge/ -count=100 -timeout 15m -run 'TestOnlyTheStepsTheProviderRefusedAreReportedRefused' | grep -c '^--- FAIL' prints 19. Its sibling TestTheBridgeReportsEveryTurnItEndsCleanAndRefusedAlike prints 0 over the same 100 runs, so the harness is not generally unstable. It also failed once in my full-suite run (daemon-full12.log, internal/claudebridge 4.562s), which is how I found it, and go test -race over 10 runs reports no data race. The failure is always the same: turnoutcome_test.go:143 reads {Generation:4 Sequence:2 Outcome:refused Message:Claude Code: error_during_execution API Error: 529 overloaded} where the test wants the turn clean. The mechanism is in the fake provider, bridge_test.go:143-158: the 'fail-then' case dials the inbox socket, writes the delivery and deliberately does not wait for it ('The delivery is sent and not waited on'), then emits the refused result immediately. bridge.go:653 ends the turn at that step unless 'stepped && len(b.queue) > 0', so whether the turn continues into the clean second step depends on whether the delivery has reached b.queue by the time the result is handled. When it loses that race the turn genuinely ended at the refused step and the bridge's report is truthful about the turn it ended - which is why I am reporting this as one finding and not two: what is undecided is the design, not just the test. bridge.go:608-611 states the rule as 'a step that ran clears what an earlier failed one left, since the provider answered after all', and that rule is silent on a delivery still in flight when the step fails. Either the bridge waits for an in-flight delivery before it ends the turn, which makes the rule hold as written and the test deterministic, or the design says an in-flight delivery may lose and the test must synchronise before emitting the failure. I did not write a red test for this: a deterministic test can only be written once that choice is made, since the passing and failing orders are both reachable from the same inputs today, and bridge.go:144-147 records why the fake cannot simply read the delivery's answer there. The stake is the one the test's own comment names: 'Counting either would walk a working claim to the launch failure limit, fail it, and abandon the session it is working in'.

proof.criterion: Item 3 (the architect's) - whether this branch's timestamped migrations still apply when INFRA-484's #2538, whose stamp 20261029195520 sorts after every one of them, merges first; that is, whether whichever pull request merges second must be restamped.
proof.surface: The store's real Migrate path over the pod's own PostgreSQL 18.6, driven with the real embedded migration set rather than crafted migrations, through store.migrate - the same function Migrate calls.
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && go test -overlay $TMPDIR/probe12/overlay.json ./internal/store/ -count=1 -run 'TestProbeThisBranchsEarlierStampsApplyAfterInfra484sLaterOne' -v, with LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN naming a database legion_test owns. The probe splits the real embedded set into the 67 numbered migrations both branches share and this branch's 13 timestamped ones, migrates a database with the shared set plus INFRA-484's real stamp alone, then migrates again with this branch's 13 earlier stamps added.
proof.observed: PASS. 'shared (numbered) = 67, this branch's timestamped = 13'; the first migrate applied 68 of 68 and left schema_version at 20261029195520; the second applied exactly 13 - every one of this branch's earlier-stamped migrations - each recorded exactly once; the reported version stayed at the highest stamp; a third migrate applied 0. Answer: neither pull request needs restamping, whichever merges first. The reason is in store.go:198 apply, which asks versionRecorded for that migration's own version rather than comparing against the highest recorded one, so an earlier stamp arriving after a later one is applied rather than skipped.
proof.negativeControl: The probe refuses its own premise rather than passing vacuously: it fails if any of this branch's timestamped migrations sorts at or after 20261029195520, and it fails if the second migrate applies any count other than 13, which is what a skipped earlier stamp would produce.

notesForNextRound: The claudebridge race is the one open item. Driving it is cheap and does not need the full suite: go test ./internal/claudebridge/ -count=100 -run 'TestOnlyTheStepsTheProviderRefusedAreReportedRefused' takes about a minute and prints a failure count, so the next round can judge a fix by that count rather than by one green run. One green run means nothing here: the test passes 81 times in 100.

Whatever the fix, check it against the design question and not only the count. A fix that synchronises the fake makes the count 0 while leaving the bridge's behaviour for an in-flight delivery exactly as it is; a fix in the bridge changes that behaviour. Both reach 0, and only the second makes bridge.go:608-611's rule true as written.

The harness ordering, twice learned: start NATS before the suite, not after. Build a database legion_test owns (psql -tAc 'create database <name> owner legion_test') rather than pointing tests at the pod DSN's own postgres database, where internal/daemon's migrations fail at 0001_init with 'permission denied for schema public'.

Read each bun file's skip count, never its pass count. The gates are LEGION_TEST_OMP, LEGION_TEST_NATS_URL and LEGION_TEST_CLAUDE; claude-envoy's skips rose from 13 to 16 this round, which is new tests behind LEGION_TEST_CLAUDE rather than a regression, but it is worth re-reading rather than assuming.

Two failures in the list are main's and not this branch's - TestSessionsImportRefusesSymlinkedSessionDirectory, which I proved at origin/main in this pod, and TestACarriedOrphanUnderAReopenedOldRootStillGetsItsSlot, which is #2226's and flakes only under load.
